 Snapdragon chipsets confirmed for the Samsung Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra, but there is a catch
 ⓘ Notebookcheck With an extra model inbound for the S27 series, Samsung appears to have split its Snapdragon chips between the Pro and Ultra (Galaxy S26 pictured). New import-export records name the chipsets in the international variants of all four Galaxy S27 models, with the Pro being powered by an unexpected chipset. Bùi Giang , Published 11/04/2026 🇩🇪 🇪🇸 ...

 Import-export records on the trade data platform NBD list the European variants of all four upcoming Galaxy S27 models along with their chipsets. The entries cover the SM-S952B/DS (Galaxy S27), SM-S956B/DS (Galaxy S27+), SM-S957B/DS (Galaxy S27 Pro) and SM-S958B/DS (Galaxy S27 Ultra).
 ⓘ nbd.ltd The European Samsung Galaxy S27 series shows up in import-export records 
 According to the records, the Galaxy S27 and Galaxy S27+ will use Samsung's upcoming Exynos 2700 , while the Galaxy S27 Pro is listed with the SM8950, better known by its marketing name, Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 . The Galaxy S27 Ultra gets the SM8975, Qualcomm's top-of-the-line chip for this generation, marketed as the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 . All four entries specify 12 GB of RAM and 256 GB of storage, with displays measuring 6.3 inches (S27), 6.7 inches (S27+), 6.5 inches (S27 Pro) and 6.9 inches (S27 Ultra). 
 The listing puts the Galaxy S27 Pro on a lower-tier chip than the Ultra, an arrangement similar to that of Xiaomi's 18 series: the smaller Xiaomi 18 Pro has the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 , while the larger and more expensive Xiaomi 18 Pro Max has the Extreme variant. Samsung has not announced the Galaxy S27 series, so any information should be considered preliminary until officially confirmed.
